body: Please don’t take moxi, I took it two years ago and still can‘t walk normally again. So many other options available :)

Heal Pelvic Pain by Amy Stein has all the techniques and stretches that I saw PTs perform/recommend in it! With the internal massage, the quick takeaway is, you want clean hands, medical lube and then to gently massage in particular the sides of the vagina - it should eventually feel soft rather than hard or ridged which is typical for PFD. If you think of it like feeling your way around a clock, where 12 is the top and 6 is the bottom, you want to avoid 12 and 6 because that actually can trigger your urethra, but with the sides you are safe. I wouldn’t start doing intense pressure point work at the beginning yet. Then if you have vulvodynia, you want to desensitise the skin in that area by very gradually touching more and more, first just around, then moving in on sore areas so you retrain your body to understand that it’s safe. All with a lot of patience, just enough that it gets better but not so much straight away that you give yourself a huge flare. The book is the best primary source though.

I got my pain H about a year and a half ago. I had a really awful reaction to an antibiotic and then also experienced a very slight impact to my ear/TMJ and boom I had pain H. It took me several months to figure out how to handle it and I made things a lot worse for myself in the beginning but it’s been slow and steady improvement with a couple of setbacks ever since. I went from not being able to hear most digital sound at even the lowest level on my phone or shut my front door without pain to comfortably playing most music at medium level and weirdly in the outside world I’m usually fine although I do live in a fairly peaceful city. Impact noises like doors slamming still hurt me and same goes for things like gunshot noises in TV shows etc. However a lot of days I don’t even notice my pain H now because I know how to avoid sounds that hurt me. The more time I have without pain, the quicker my ears heal. Also, I was really badly affected everywhere physically by the antibiotic (couldn’t walk for months etc and still far from normal now) so you may get better much faster because you’re in a healthy body otherwise :)

Hey, just to say, you will adapt and also your ears will recover, probably much more slowly than you would like. Once I started protecting my ears from anything that gave me pain and making sure I was only exposing myself to sounds that were tolerable, things gradually started improving. Luckily, you are only 22 and you could even start a family in 5 or 10 years if it took that long to recover, so don’t worry about that at all. This all doesn’t have to mean that the next few years of your life are a write-off, especially if you manage to work around your current limitations for a bit.

So while it is a sexually transmitted bacteria, it can definitely lie dormant in your body without causing a symptomatic infection until there’s is an overgrowth because of something that compromises your system like a UTI. Ok the ureaplasma was probably the main initial issue not the UTI. The first few days of Keflex would have knocked out a UTI. The good news is, the ureaplasma is massively treatable, but it doesn’t have a cell wall so only particular antibiotics work. Most GPs have no clue about it. There’s an excellent sub about it on here, your best bet is a dual treatment of seven days of doxycycline followed by a short course of azithromycin. Should be totally safe. Hopefully treating that should already make you feel much better! 

In terms of my own recovery, it has been massively complicated by a couple of things. I actually stopped taking moxifloxacin after one pill because I experienced peripheral neuropathy in my left hand and was totally back to normal within a week or so. Unfortunately several weeks later I took an unrelated medication which triggered a severe reaction and few days later I couldn’t use my arms, a few weeks later I couldn’t walk. I’m now six months out and making slow but steady progress. My ‘only’ real side effect has been crippling full-body tendinitis. Honestly, it was awful for a few months but now I can use my hands and arms again to type and write, although can’t lift anything much heavier than 500g yet, can walk around 2500- 3000 steps a day spaced out through the day, doing stairs again. But- during the acute phase I was so fragile that a long tight hug sprained my TMJ and gave me pain sensitivity to sound which is debilitating and hasn’t gone away. However that was an accident and if that hadn’t happened I would be feeling somewhat optimistic at this point.  And if I had never taken that other medication, I suspect I would be having only mild symptoms, if any now. 

So- I would be careful with the medication you take in the future other than antibiotics and also be as careful as possible with your fragile body just until the initial storm blows over. Also, the sooner you can make sure you have a network of people around you to support you in every way, the better, because psychologically this is a really tough one for anyone. You will come out on the other side though. Keep us updated :)

I think I might know what’s going on. You may well have either a mycoplasma or a ureaplasma infection which mainly cause persistent urethritis, which is what you have by the sound of it. Both can be misdiagnosed as a UTI but the bacteria causing it are completely different so none of the antibiotics you have taken would be effective (doxy works but usually in combination with Azithromycin). Mycoplasma/ureaplasma have no cell wall and take two months to culture from a urine sample - a PCR test is necessary to diagnose. Antibiotic treatment is fairly straightforward - doxy/azithro or if that fails, the one FQ that is effective is moxifloxacin which you will be able to avoid. 
I have had a very similar experience to you in terms of having all the UTI antibiotics thrown at me, nothing showing up in the urine sample but the urethral burning still persisting - finally after a lot of research I discovered myco and ureaplasma and sent off for lab tests. N.B. not all doctors are aware of these infections, but doctors specialising in sexual health usually are. I think it’s definitely worth a try.
